summary: Tested the auto-shrink body_leading retry wrapper in build_letter_pdf() and the signature-split fix, using /api/letters/preview-pdf, issue, PDF and DOCX, plus a light UI regression on /letters. Results: (1) The main agent's scan (~12-word paragraphs) matches the claim. Counts 8-15 fit on 1 page, 16-17 are the known orphan edge, and 18+ paginate with body text on the last page. (2) I swept 1-20 paragraphs of ~17 words each (2 lines) across 5 signature variants: rich default, rich + signature image, classic, classic + image, and a 3-line rich signature. Title, name and extra line were NEVER split across pages, and X-Sig-Page always matched the page the title is actually on. (3) With 2-line paragraphs, the residual orphan window is n=9 (plain), or n=8-9 when a signature image is set. This is the same documented edge as 16-17 short paragraphs, because the edge depends on line count, not paragraph count. I confirmed that every attempt down to 0.7x (1.05) still orphans at n=9, so falling back to 1.0x is correct. (4) Short letters (3 paragraphs) give the same paragraph y-positions as an explicit body_leading=1.5, so nothing is compressed, and they respond in about 0.15s. Worst-case retry requests take 0.5-2.0s. (5) For n=4, 14 and 22, the issued PDF matches the preview (page count, signature page, paragraph positions), and DOCX returns 200 and is a valid zip. (6) Regression suites pass: test_letters_multipage_iter136, test_letters_drafts, test_letters_manual_custom_columns and test_letters_iter137_fixes (20 tests). (7) UI check: 14 paragraphs show no pager and the drag handle on page 0. 25 paragraphs show the pager as 'صفحة 1 من 2', with no handle on page 1 and the handle above the signature after clicking next.

minor.issue: Each retry only compresses line leading. Paragraph gap (para_gap=3), gap_closing and gap_signature stay fixed, so the rescue window is narrow (1-2 paragraph counts still orphan). At 0.7x the in-paragraph lines also get visibly tight (for example the 8 x 2-line paragraph case). This is design feedback, not a bug.

Every page PNG request re-runs up to 7 renders (about 1.7-2s in edge cases), and the UI pager fetches each page separately. Caching the chosen leading or PDF per payload would avoid repeating this work.

action_items: Optional: also shrink gap_closing/gap_signature/para_gap in the later retries to narrow the residual orphan window further.
Optional: note in the docs that the '8-15 paragraphs' figure applies only to 1-line paragraphs.
critical_code_review_comments: The orphan check uses body_end_page_idx, captured before the closing. If the closing alone moves to the next page with the signature, it counts as an orphan, which is acceptable.
The signature reservation is 20mm (34mm with an image). A rich signature section with 4+ lines could still exceed it. 3 lines tested OK.

In the rich-signature + image path, the image is drawn at y-16mm after the rich section with no extra ensure(), so a tall section could push the image toward BOTTOM_SAFE. It was not observed in tests.
seed_data_creation: Issued 3 TEST_autoshrink letters (n=4, 14, 22). Issued letters cannot be deleted.
context_for_next_testing_agent: Main regression: pytest backend/tests/test_letters_autoshrink_leading_iter138.py (10 tests, about 80s). It sweeps 1-20 paragraphs of 17 words across 5 signature variants (signature image injected through letterhead_override.signature_base64; sections={} forces the classic signature path) and allows an orphan window of at most 2 counts. scan_autoshrink_iter138.py shows the orphan threshold against explicit leading values. UI: use letter-signatory-select='__manual__'. The body editor is a contenteditable inside [data-testid=letter-body]; set it with execCommand insertHTML.
